overview: This 153-page file documents Parker Pen Company’s efforts to protect fountain pen inventions and the PARKER trademark in Japan during the 1930s. Petitions, patents, Japanese bureau notices, opposition decisions, correspondence, drawings, and advertising trace rejected applications and challenges to competing marks. U.S. officials found no evidence of discrimination but considered whether diplomatic intervention had another basis.
interest: Technical exhibits and Japanese decisions show how Parker contested patent rejections and rival marks while seeking U.S. diplomatic support.
